[Highway Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00387) use input-dependent transform/carry gates, commonly coupled as y=T(x)H(x)+(1−T(x))x; negative transform biases initially favor carrying the input. A NextItNet block y=h+gF(h) instead preserves the additive skip while conditionally scaling its residual. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) uses a learned, input-independent scalar initialized at zero; [LayerScale](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.17239) uses input-independent per-channel scales initialized near zero. Both suppress initial residual contributions. [Hierarchical Gating Networks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.09217) already provide user-conditioned sigmoid feature and instance selection in sequential recommendation, although their gates filter history representations rather than NextItNet residual branches.

Direct algebra: with z=[h;u;e;c] and W=0, g=σ(Wz+2)/σ(2)=1. This initializes the gate to identity scaling, preserving the original NextItNet block; it does not initialize the block to the identity map. Residual weights receive ordinary initial gradients, whereas ReZero initially blocks residual-branch parameter gradients and LayerScale attenuates them. The normalized gate’s initial logit derivative is 1−σ(2)≈0.1192; the unnormalized sigmoid derivative is ≈0.1050, versus its maximum 0.25. Bias two therefore gives moderate saturation, not a dead gate. Scaling lies in (0,1.1353), allowing much stronger suppression than amplification. At W=0, gate weights can learn immediately, but conditioning features initially receive no gradient through the gate itself.

Interpretation: novelty would concern the particular causal conditioning and integration, rather than conditional gating generally. A four-item causal mean adds an explicit local summary but may duplicate information already encoded by NextItNet’s receptive field; e may also overlap with h, depending on its definition. Test conditioning ablations against a learned static scale under identical validation settings; redundancy and optimization benefits remain empirical hypotheses.
